thread:
carmen: quick flag  int8 run of rwd-v3.5-mini in canary (7%) shows rerank anchor NDCG softening on multi-pass longchains (~3.8% drift). short traffic is fine.
todd: link: https://dash.internal/redwood/onboard/rwd-v3.5-mini/int8  seems focused on multi-pass retrieval where candidate duplication is high.
mei: any latency wins?
carmen: p95 latency -8ms. CPU tail for rerank workers unchanged. main concern is quality delta on the "dup-heavy" cohort.
ops-runner: suggest policy: "safety-split" that routes only the high-risk cohort to fp32 and keeps the rest on int8. avoids full rollback.
mei: +1. also we should wire a "safety_thermostat" so the canary weight autoshrinks if ndcg_delta exceeds threshold for sustained time. want config snippet?
todd: yes paste it.
mei: snippet (add to rollout-policy.json):
```json
{
  "policy_name": "safety_split_thermostat",
  "match": {
    "tokens_gt": 1200,
    "dup_score_gt": 0.6
  },
  "action": {
    "route_to": "rwd-v3.4-fp32",
    "shadow": true
  },
  "thermostat": {
    "metric": "ndcg_delta",
    "threshold": 0.03,
    "window_mins": 15,
    "shrink_factor": 0.5
  }
}
```
ops-runner: infra-bot will create an autoscaling/pause hook tied to the thermostat. if thermostat trips, it will scale canary by shrink_factor every window until under threshold.
infra-bot: hook created: THERMOSTAT_1754329999. will post alerts to #eng-oncall and page on sustained trip.
carmen: plan: change canary 7%->2%, deploy safety_split_thermostat, enable extra shadowing for dup-heavy cohort for 12h. collect more samples and run replay.
todd: owner: mei for 12h watch, carmen will attach replay traces and rwd-eval job will add dup-heavy cohort to nightly.
mei: PR opened for rollout config: https://git.internal/redwood/rollout-config/pull/517. keeping an eye on p50/p95 latency for rerouted requests.
ops-runner: added telemetry guard: if routed_errors > 0.7% or p95_latency_increase > 120ms for 10m then pause canary and notify.
carmen: applying change now. will post back in 3h with early telemetry. if anything looks bad we full-rollback to v3.4.
mei: thanks all. :ok_hand:
